title: Provisional Priamurye Government
capsule: The Provisional Priamurye Government was a short-lived White Russian enclave in the Russian Far East, established in Vladivostok on 27 May 1921 following a coup by Kappelevtsy—remnants of General Vladimir Kappel's forces—operating under Japanese military protection against the Soviet-aligned Far Eastern Republic. The Merkulov brothers (Spiridon and Nikolai) led initially until General Mikhail Diterikhs replaced them in June 1922, styling himself voyevoda and convening a Zemsky Sobor that symbolically called for restoration of the Romanov dynasty. When Japan withdrew its forces in late 1922, Soviet troops retook most of the territory; the surrender of General Anatoly Pepelyayev in June 1923 ended the last armed White resistance of the Russian Civil War. The government is recorded as formally dissolved on 16 June 1923.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory around Vladivostok is well-attested; the nominal claim to wider Priamurye was largely theoretical given Japanese-dependent military capacity.
